summary: A target-level construction of the simplicial support tower on actual perfect-complex K-theory spectra over a perfect field, with moving, localisation, functoriality, the cycle-complex equivalence for its layers, and comparison with Levine’s global coherent model and the Friedlander–Suslin support tower and cycle layer. Ordinary codimension coniveau, perfect complexes, cycle complexes, relative cycles and general spectra remain with their established owners. No spectral sequence is used to define the tower.

nodes.title: Facewise admissible supports
nodes.statement: For a smooth separated k-scheme X, S_X^p(n) is the inclusion poset of closed subsets W of X × Δ^n such that, for every nonempty face F (including Δ^n), every irreducible component of W ∩ (X × F) has codimension at least p in X × F. Empty intersections impose no condition. On disconnected X the condition is componentwise. For a finite family C of locally closed pure-codimension strata and e:C→ℕ, S_X,C,e^p(n) consists of W∈S_X^p(n) which additionally have codimension at least p−e(C) inside C × F, with a nonpositive bound vacuous; write S_X,C^p for e=0; for maps f_i:Y_i → X, S_X,{f_i}^p(n) requires W ∈ S_X^p(n) and (f_i × id)⁻¹W ∈ S_Yi^p(n) for every i. These are subposets closed under passage to smaller closed supports and finite unions. On an affine chart with coordinate ring R and simplex coordinates t_0,…,t_n, put I_τ=(t_i : i∉τ) for a nonempty set τ of vertices. A support V(J) is admissible exactly when every prime P of R/I_τ containing the image of J has height at least p, for every τ.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Use the already owned algebraic simplex and its face embeddings; impose a codimension condition on each face, rather than just on the ambient product.

Check inverse images along cofaces by composing faces and along codegeneracies by their affine-space fibres. Empty support is initial and finite union gives upper bounds, so each support poset is filtered.

The affine description is the prime-height criterion for codimension in each face ring. Radical ideals define the same support condition; the image ideal, not its height in the original ring, is used after restriction.
acceptance: For p=0 every closed support is admissible.
In degree n=0 this is the support poset of the ordinary codimension filtration, without identifying its degree-zero value with the realised tower.

sources.match: Defines the facewise support poset and its refinement adapted to a morphism.
Support conditions are downward closed and finite-union closed; additional strata impose good position.

nodes.title: The homotopy-coniveau tower and its layers
nodes.statement: Fix a presheaf E of fibrant ordinary spectra on smooth k-schemes, reduced on the empty scheme and carrying finite disjoint unions to products. For Y smooth and W closed put E^W(Y)=hofib(E(Y)→E(Y∖W)), with the canonical support-enlargement maps. Define E^(p)(X,n)=hocolim_{W∈S_X^p(n)} E^W(X×Δ^n), and E^(p)(X)=|n↦E^(p)(X,n)| as a derived geometric realisation. The inclusions S^(p+1)⊂S^(p) give a tower; L_E^p(X)=hocofib(E^(p+1)(X)→E^(p)(X)). Restricted support families give the analogous objects. For E=K use SchemeKTheoryOperations’ actual nonconnective K-spectrum of Perf; its localisation equivalence identifies E^W with K(X×Δ^n on W). There is an augmentation E(X)→E^(0)(X) induced by the projections X×Δ^n→X. No E₂ page or groups chosen in advance enter these definitions.
hypotheses: E is a presheaf of ordinary spectra on Sm/k, replaced functorially by fibrant spectra; the support posets are taken in a fixed universe.
For the K-specialisation X is smooth separated finite type over a perfect field; all open complements are quasi-compact.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Take functorial homotopy fibres and the support-enlargement maps. Use the filtered support posets and their simplex inverse-image functors to obtain a simplicial diagram of spectra.
Use the requested small-diagram homotopy-colimit and realisation interface, with derived replacements and cofinality, to define its total spectrum and tower maps.
Form layers in spectra. The fibre sequence E^(p+1)→E^(p)→L_E^p is the stable fibre/cofibre triangle; its connecting map belongs to this triangle, before any spectral-sequence indexing.
acceptance: K^(p)(X,0) agrees with S.4’s ordinary codimension-support spectrum; realisation is an additional operation.
The realisation and cofibres are performed in spectra, not by replacing each support spectrum by its K₀ group.

sources.match: The tower is a realisation of supported spectra; successive layers are homotopy cofibres.
The K-theory version uses the same simplex support filtration and compares with a coherent model.

nodes.title: K-theory satisfies the support-theory axioms
nodes.statement: On smooth schemes over k, perfect-complex nonconnective K-theory is A¹-invariant, sends elementary Nisnevich distinguished squares to homotopy-cartesian squares, and has connective supported spectra K(Y on W). For a finite Galois extension k′/k of degree d, restriction K(Y)[1/d]→(K(Y_{k′})[1/d])^{hGal(k′/k)} is an equivalence. The same transfer argument applies with the support conditions carried along. Thus the integral tower theorems below apply also to finite perfect fields: inversion of d is an auxiliary step in the moving proof, removed using extensions of coprime degrees.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Regularity gives K=G and K(Y on W)≃G(W), so negative supported groups vanish; ordinary K of singular W is not substituted for G(W).
Import homotopy invariance and Nisnevich excision from S.4–S.5.

For the finite étale extension use transfer and base change: cor∘res=d and res∘cor=Σ_g g. After inverting d these identify invariant homotopy groups. The homotopy-fixed-point comparison in the category of ℤ[1/d]-local spectra follows by averaging, not by assuming integral Galois descent.

For supported diagrams, replace a support over k′ by the finite union of its Galois translates. These invariant supports form a cofinal family and descend to k without changing facewise codimension. The transfer identities therefore apply to the support homotopy colimits as well.
For a finite base field use two sufficiently large finite extensions of coprime degrees to kill the moving obstruction integrally, as in the transfer part of Levine’s moving argument.
acceptance: For a finite field the output remains integral; no blanket inversion of char k is introduced.
For a singular closed W in smooth Y the connective support theory is G(W), not K(W).

sources.match: States and verifies the required axioms for K-theory.

sources.locator: §4.1, pp. 25–27, and coprime-degree descent in Proposition 3.3.4, pp. 23–24
sources.match: The Galois condition is used after inverting extension degrees and then combined with transfer descent.

nodes.title: Moving supports into prescribed good position
nodes.statement: Let C be a finite collection of locally closed pure-codimension subsets of X and let E be A¹-invariant, Nisnevich excisive and satisfy the finite-field transfer axiom of k-support-axioms when k is finite. The inclusion E_C^(p)(−)→E^(p)(−) is a Nisnevich-local equivalence of presheaves on X. If U⊂X is affine, E_C^(p)(U)→E^(p)(U) is an equivalence of spectra; over a field it is also a Zariski-local equivalence. Given finitely many maps f_i:Y_i→X between smooth schemes, supports can be moved into a common refinement adapted to all f_i. The equivalence concerns the realised restricted tower, not a cofinality assertion about the original degreewise support posets.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: On affine space use generic translations and the explicit algebraic homotopies, retaining good position on all faces and on the finitely many additional strata.

For a smooth affine X pass through a presentation and the projecting-cone argument; Nisnevich excision compares supports in the étale neighbourhood. Filter a finite family of morphisms by fibre dimensions using generic flatness to obtain enough strata for every inverse image.
Carry out the argument for finite collections of supports and homotopies, then pass to the homotopy colimit. Use the coprime-degree transfer argument over finite fields.
State global equivalence only after the descent step; the local theorem alone does not identify global sections.
acceptance: For the inclusion of a rational point into A¹, the unrestricted codimension-one support consisting of that point has no codimension-one inverse image. Moving replaces the support family before pullback.
No claim says the good-position family is degreewise cofinal: an inadmissibly positioned support cannot be repaired merely by enlarging it.

sources.match: Supplies local moving, its affine strengthening over a field and the translation/projecting-cone proof.
Uses supports adapted to morphisms to construct the functorial tower.

nodes.title: Localisation and excision of the support tower
nodes.statement: Let j:U→X be open with closed complement Z. Put E_Z^(p)(X,n)=hocolim_{W∈S_X^p(n), W⊂Z×Δ^n} E^W(X×Δ^n). For a theory satisfying the moving hypotheses, realisation gives a fibre sequence E_Z^(p)(X)→E^(p)(X)→E^(p)(U). The construction is natural for open restrictions and support enlargements, and gives the corresponding sequence of layers. An étale map X′→X inducing an isomorphism over Z induces E_Z^(p)(X)≃E_Z′^(p)(X′). Consequently the tower and its layers satisfy elementary Nisnevich excision and Zariski Mayer–Vietoris; their maps to derived sections on X_Zar are equivalences for the finite-dimensional noetherian X in scope.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: For each degree first restrict U to the family of supports that extend to an admissible support on X. Nested-support localisation identifies the fibre with supports contained in Z.
Apply the moving/localisation argument to compare the extendable-support realisation on U with the unrestricted one. Do not identify their degreewise posets or spectra.

Derived filtered homotopy colimits and realisation preserve the finite stable fibre sequences by the requested spectrum interface. Apply the same argument to adjacent tower maps to obtain the layer sequence.

For the étale excision map compare the supported spectra before taking homotopy colimits. Brown–Gersten descent on the finite-dimensional noetherian site upgrades the resulting distinguished squares to the asserted equivalence with derived sections.
acceptance: For p=0 and E=K this recovers S.3’s localisation sequence K(X on Z)→K(X)→K(U).
For Z=∅ the fibre is contractible; for Z=X and U=∅ it is the whole level.
The theorem preserves codimension measured in X; no formula K_Z^(p)(X)=K^(p)(Z) is asserted.

sources.match: Compares extendable supports to all supports and gives the realised localisation sequence.
The coherent version has localisation and Mayer–Vietoris, which globalise the supported construction.

nodes.title: A functorial replacement of the whole tower
nodes.statement: For E as in moving-with-constraints, construct a contravariant functor X↦𝒯_E(X) from Sm/k to the category of towers of spectra and a natural augmentation to the constant tower E. Its restriction to smooth maps is equivalent, as a tower, to p↦E^(p)(X). For an arbitrary f:Y→X, the induced map is represented in the homotopy category by E^(p)(X) ← E^(p)(X)_f → E^(p)(Y), where the first arrow is the moving equivalence and the second is support pullback. The replacements for all p and all maps are chosen together, so composition is coherent and transitions and layer triangles are natural. When E=K the p=0 map is the usual derived pullback of perfect complexes.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Use the category of simultaneous adapted support conditions over a scheme and its finite diagrams of maps. The moving theorem compares each such refinement to the unrestricted local tower.

Apply the requested homotopy-coherent diagram replacement to the tower-valued diagram, followed by a Nisnevich-fibrant replacement. Carry the transition maps and the augmentation throughout this operation.

Use localisation/descent to compare the resulting values with the raw support realisations. On smooth maps and at weight zero the original pullbacks already preserve the supports, giving the stated comparisons.
acceptance: An inverse to a moving equivalence is taken in the coherent diagram category; independent arbitrary inverses for each p do not constitute this construction.

sources.match: Constructs all tower maps together and records naturality, fibre-sequence preservation and functoriality.
Uses adapted supports and a diagram regularisation to obtain the presheaf construction.

nodes.title: Homotopy invariance of the tower
nodes.statement: For E satisfying the moving hypotheses, projection pullback E^(p)(X)→E^(p)(X×A¹) and L_E^p(X)→L_E^p(X×A¹) are equivalences, natural as maps of towers. In particular E(X)→E^(0)(X) is an equivalence if E is A¹-invariant. These statements concern the derived realisations; they do not say that every degreewise restricted support spectrum is invariant.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Restrict to supports in simultaneous good position for the zero and unit sections and the algebraic contraction of A¹.
Use the simplicial homotopy induced by multiplication on A¹ to compare section followed by projection with the identity; moving gives equivalence with the unrestricted realisations.
For p=0 the maximal support X×Δ^n is terminal, so the level is E(X×Δ^n). A¹-invariance makes the augmentation a levelwise equivalence from the constant spectrum.
acceptance: For K this identifies the bottom stage with the K-spectrum, rather than with its Eilenberg–MacLane K₀ truncation.

sources.match: Proves homotopy invariance with the support conditions retained.
Gives the augmentation and its homotopy-invariance consequence.

nodes.title: Semilocal simplices and multirelative face fibres
nodes.statement: For a field F/k, let R_{n,F} be the localisation of F[t_0,…,t_n]/(Σt_i−1) at the multiplicative set of functions nonzero at each of the n+1 vertices. Write Δ^n_{0,F}=Spec R_{n,F}. The nonempty faces form the punctured (n+1)-cube; evaluating a presheaf E on all these faces and taking the total homotopy fibre defines E(Δ^n_{0,F},∂). This is the multirelative face object. The closed union ∂Δ^n_{0,F}=V(t_0⋯t_n) is a different object, and its ordinary relative fibre is not identified with the face-cube fibre without a closed-descent theorem. Extend E to these semilocal schemes and to finitely generated residue fields by filtered neighbourhoods.
hypotheses: F is a finitely generated extension of the perfect base field k; n≥0.
The presheaf is extended by filtered neighbourhoods; K-continuity supplies its concrete ring interpretation.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Localise at the complement of the union of the vertex maximal ideals. This is simultaneous semilocalisation, not the product of the separate local rings.
Intersect faces after this localisation, discard the empty intersection of all faces, and form the total homotopy fibre of the resulting finite cube.
For theories initially on Sm/k, use the neighbourhood extension and the requested filtered-colimit compatibility. For K this extension agrees with actual K of the localised ring by continuity.
acceptance: The face-cube fibre must remain distinct from the ordinary pair (R,R/(t_0⋯t_n)) until the specific KH comparison is invoked.

sources.match: Defines the vertex semilocalisation and the multirelative face cube; the criterion uses this cube.

nodes.title: Well-connected support theories
nodes.statement: For an A¹-invariant Nisnevich-excisive presheaf E satisfying the finite-field transfer axiom, define Ω_T E(Y)=E^{Y×{0}}(Y×P¹). A theory is well-connected if (i) E^W(Y) is connective for every smooth Y and closed W, and (ii) for every d≥0 and every finitely generated field extension F/k, (Ω_T^d E)^(0/1)(F) has homotopy only in degree zero. Here (0/1) denotes the actual adjacent tower cofibre, not the pointwise Postnikov truncation. The canonical map from π₀(Ω_T^d E(F)) identifies that group with π₀ of this zero layer. Iterated Ω_T is defined on presheaves before forming its coniveau tower.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Define the T-loop theory by the ordinary supported fibre on P¹, and iterate it. A¹-invariance identifies it with the fibre of evaluation at infinity when required.
State connectivity with the convention π_i=0 for i<0. Impose the fieldwise zero-layer condition for every iterate of Ω_T.
Identify π₀ via the semilocal-simplex presentation and the constant π₀ maps; the stronger multirelative criterion is a separate theorem.
acceptance: Knowing only that E(F) is connective does not establish well-connectedness: supported connectivity and every T-loop zero-layer test are required.

sources.locator: Definition 3.3.1 and Remarks 3.3.2, pp. 18–19; Definition 6.1.1 and Lemma 6.1.3, pp. 30–31
sources.match: Specifies the T-loop operation and both well-connectedness requirements, including the canonical degree-zero identification.

uses.how: Turns the field coefficient spectra in the layer model into Eilenberg–MacLane spectra.
Provides a checkable multirelative criterion instead of assuming the cycle-layer conclusion.

nodes.title: Purity and the T-loop shift of coniveau
nodes.statement: Let E satisfy the moving hypotheses. For p≥1, the zero section Y×{0}⊂Y×P¹ gives natural equivalences (Ω_T E)^(p−1)(Y)≃E_{Y×0}^(p)(Y×P¹)≃Ω_T(E^(p))(Y), compatible with transitions. More generally, for a smooth closed immersion i:Z→X of codimension d equipped with a trivialisation of its normal bundle, E_Z^(p)(X)≃(Ω_T^d E)^(p−d)(Z); the corresponding layer is L_{Ω_T^d E}^{p−d}(Z). A nonpositive level index is interpreted as level zero, while a layer with negative index is zero. The purity equivalence is natural for maps of trivialised pairs; a choice of normal trivialisation is not silently erased.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: For the zero section use the square defining the two support fibres and Zariski excision to identify E^{W×0} with (Ω_T E)^W; codimension shifts by one.
The localisation theorem compares the supported realised level on Y×P¹ with the T-loop of the realised level, giving the second equivalence.

For a smooth pair use Nisnevich local linearisation and deformation to the normal bundle. A¹-invariance identifies the restrictions at the two fibres of the deformation; use the specified trivialisation and iterate the zero-section calculation.
Use the fibre sequences for adjacent levels to obtain the layer formula. The negative-layer convention records that both adjacent levels have already become the same level zero.
acceptance: At p=d the supported layer is the zero layer of Ω_T^d E on Z.
For K, regular-support dévissage and the projective-bundle basis normalise the T-loop equivalence so a point class has rank +1.
A rank-d bundle is not trivialised by one nonzero section when d>1; no such step is used.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.3.4, pp. 19–20; Lemma 4.2.1 and Proposition 4.2.2, pp. 24–25
sources.match: Gives the T-loop shift and purity with a chosen trivialisation; these are the local inputs for the layer reduction.

nodes.title: The multirelative criterion for well-connectedness
nodes.statement: Assume E is A¹-invariant, Nisnevich excisive, satisfies the finite-field axiom and has connective supported spectra. Then E is well-connected if and only if π₀((Ω_T^d E)(Δ^n_{0,F},∂))=0 for every n≥1, d≥0 and finitely generated field F/k. The zero-layer coefficient is canonically π₀Ω_T^d E(F). The condition is on the total face-cube fibre, not just on K₀ of the semilocal scheme.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: Use the semilocal-simplex presentation of the zero layer. Connectivity and the degeneracy splittings identify its π₀ with π₀E(F).

Replace E by its positive Postnikov cover after separating the constant π₀ part. The total face-cube calculation identifies the obstruction to positive homotopy in the realisation with its multirelative degree-zero groups.
Apply the same argument to Ω_T^d E; purity identifies its supported fibres and supplies the required connectivity for every d. This proves both implications without presupposing a cycle equivalence.
acceptance: The case n=0 is excluded: for K it has π₀K(F)=ℤ rather than zero.

sources.match: Proves the criterion using face cubes and Postnikov covers of connective theories.

nodes.title: Well-connectedness of algebraic K-theory
nodes.statement: The K-theory presheaf on smooth schemes over a perfect field is well-connected. The projective-bundle/zero-section equivalence identifies Ω_T^d K with K, with rank-one class +1. For every finitely generated F/k and n≥1, π₀K(Δ^n_{0,F},∂)=0. Consequently (Ω_T^d K)^(0/1)(F)≃Hℤ canonically by rank, for all d≥0. This is an equivalence of coefficient spectra; it does not assert K(F)≃Hℤ.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Supported connectivity comes from K(Y on W)≃G(W). The projective-bundle theorem and restriction at infinity identify each T-loop of K with K.

Use the S.5 request for KH closed descent and the low-degree K→KH comparison on the normal-crossing boundary D=V(t_0⋯t_n) of R=R_{n,F}. It identifies the degree-zero multirelative group with the degree-zero ordinary relative group and gives exactness K₁(R)→K₁(D)→K₀(R,∂)→K₀(R)→K₀(D).

The map GL(R)→GL(R/I) is surjective for semilocal R and I=(t_0⋯t_n)⊂Jac(R), hence K₁(R)→K₁(D) is onto. K₀(R)=ℤ and its map to K₀(D) is injective: composing with evaluation at any vertex gives the rank isomorphism K₀(R)→ℤ. Only injectivity is needed; for n=1 the target is ℤ², not ℤ.
The exact sequence gives the required vanishing. Apply the semilocal criterion and the uniqueness of the zero Postnikov spectrum with π₀=ℤ to obtain the coefficient equivalence.
acceptance: For n=1, K₀(R)→K₀(F×F) is the injective diagonal; the same relative vanishing follows.
The KH step is a requested proof input; the tower and the output theorem still concern ordinary K-theory.

sources.match: Uses supported G-theory, T-loop invariance, the normal-crossing KH comparison and semilocal relative K₀ vanishing. The rank argument here corrects the boundary-K₀ assertion recorded in sourceIssues.

nodes.title: Idempotence and orthogonality of coniveau layers
nodes.statement: For E satisfying the moving hypotheses over a perfect field and 0≤a≤b, the canonical comparison maps (E^(a))^(b)→E^(b) and (E^(b))^(a)→E^(b) are equivalences. For all a,b≥0, L_{L_E^b}^a is zero if a≠b and is equivalent to L_E^b if a=b. The comparisons are natural in E and respect the tower maps. Here the second coniveau operation is applied to the functorial presheaf furnished by functorial-tower, not to a single spectrum made into a constant presheaf.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
Every theory E under discussion is reduced on the empty scheme and sends finite disjoint unions to products of spectra; all constructions are derived.
proofSteps: On the vertex-semilocal simplex an admissible positive-codimension closed support is empty. Moving and the bisimplicial contraction turn this observation into the vanishing of the zero layer of E^(p), p>0.
Use purity and noetherian stratification by smooth pieces with trivial normal bundle to propagate this vanishing to layers of indices below p and to layers of E^(p/p+1) above p.

Apply these vanishing statements to the finite range of adjacent tower triangles between indices a and b. The resulting comparison maps give the two idempotence statements and the orthogonality formula.
Interchange the two realisations using the requested homotopy-colimit Fubini equivalence; no convergence claim for an infinite tower enters this argument.
acceptance: With a=b=p, L_K^p≃(L_K^p)^(p/p+1). This replacement, not the raw degreewise quotient, is used for the pointwise rank comparison.
The argument uses only finitely many tower triangles at a time; M.6b owns infinite-tower convergence.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.2.1 and Propositions 5.2.2–5.2.3, pp. 27–28; Theorem 5.3.1, pp. 28–29
sources.match: Derives iterated-layer vanishing and idempotence from semilocal supports and purity.

nodes.title: The point-supported model of a K-theory layer
nodes.statement: For smooth X and p≥0 there is a simplicial spectrum B_X^p with |B_X^p|≃L_K^p(X), obtained by applying the pth coniveau layer again to the presheaf L_K^p. In degree n, B_X^p(n)≃∨_{x∈X^(p)(n)} (Ω_T^p K)^(0/1)(k(x))≃∨_{x∈X^(p)(n)}Hℤ, where X^(p)(n) consists of codimension-p points whose closures meet every face properly. The coefficient equivalences are normalised by rank and K-theory’s regular-support orientation. The displayed decomposition is degreewise; the face maps on B_X^p are the ones induced by the supported theory, whose agreement with cycle intersection is the separate face-rank theorem.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Idempotence replaces the layer by its own pth layer, with its genuine functorial presheaf structure.

Use localisation to discard higher-codimension pieces of each admissible support. Over the perfect field, stratify its reduced top-dimensional part by smooth pieces; shrink around each generic point until its normal bundle is trivial.

Purity and continuity identify the remaining summand with (Ω_T^p K)^(0/1)(k(x)). For K the regular-support dévissage orientation makes changes of normal coordinates act identically on the rank coefficient. This avoids assuming a trivialisation of a rank-p bundle from one nonzero section.
Use the coefficient equivalence from well-connectedness and the homotopy-colimit coproduct formula. Retain the original induced simplex maps rather than defining them by the desired cycle formula.
acceptance: The raw quotient of degreewise supported K-levels has residue-field K-spectra, with nonzero higher homotopy; it is not replaced directly by ∨Hℤ.
For p>dim X+n the degree-n point model is zero, while its realisation can have nonzero higher homotopy in other degrees.

sources.match: The iterated-layer model has field coefficient spectra and is the input to the rank comparison.
Only purity for trivialised smooth normal bundles is required in the K-specific generic-point argument.

nodes.title: The pointwise rank comparison
nodes.statement: For the point-supported model B_X^p(n), form r_{p,n}:B_X^p(n)→H(z^p(X,n)[0]) by the wedge of the coefficient rank maps (Ω_T^p K)^(0/1)(k(x))→Hℤ followed by the inclusion of the generator [closure{x}] in the already owned free admissible-cycle group. This is a pointwise equivalence of spectra. Its assembly into a simplicial comparison requires face-rank-compatibility; it is not built by declaring the induced maps to be Bloch’s face maps.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Use the canonical degree-zero rank identification on each field coefficient spectrum, and identify its zero Postnikov spectrum with Hℤ.
Use the coproduct universal property to send the x-summand to the basis vector for its closure in z^p(X,n). The index sets are the same by admissibility.
The wedge of these equivalences is an equivalence. Prove compatibility with simplex maps in the following theorem, using the actual supported pullback.
acceptance: The map sends a rank-one coherent generic class to the positive cycle generator.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.2, equation (6.4.1) and its proof, pp. 36–37
sources.match: Constructs the rank comparison degreewise and then checks its simplex naturality separately.

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap_generator
api.statement: The unit of the x coefficient maps to [closure{x}], with coefficient +1.

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap_additive

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap_equivalence

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap_support

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.pointwiseCycleMap_open
api.statement: Open restriction discards the summands whose supports disappear and agrees with restriction of admissible cycles.

tests.name: HomotopyConiveau.rank_cycle_field_zero
tests.statement: For X=Spec F, p=n=0 the coefficient map Hℤ→H z⁰(F,0)=Hℤ sends 1 to 1.

tests.name: HomotopyConiveau.rank_cycle_empty_degree
tests.statement: For X=Spec F, n=0 and p>0 both the point model B_F^p(0) and z^p(F,0) are zero.

tests.name: HomotopyConiveau.rank_cycle_double
tests.statement: For X=Spec ℚ, p=n=1, twice the rank-one class at t_0=t_1=1/2 maps to twice that cycle, rather than to its underlying reduced support.

uses.how: The rank comparison becomes the layer equivalence only after simplex compatibility.
Fixes the normalisation of the cycle generator in the layer input.

nodes.title: Rank commutes with face and degeneracy maps
nodes.statement: The maps r_{p,n} commute with all cofaces and codegeneracies of Δ^•, using the simplex maps already induced on B_X^p. At a component y of the proper intersection of an integral admissible support W with a face F, the coefficient of the pulled-back coherent class is Σ_i(−1)^i length_{O_{X×F,y}} Tor_i^{O_{X×Δ^n,y}}(O_W,y,O_{X×F,y}). The finite alternating sum agrees with the proper-intersection coefficient used by the M.4 cycle face map. Thus r_{p,•} is a simplicial equivalence. For general scheme pullback it agrees, after moving, with the cycle pullback supplied by M.5a.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: Represent a generic generator by O_W and use the supported Cartan comparison. Derived restriction to a face gives the alternating Tor class in G₀ of its inverse image.

Apply the requested general-field Serre–Tor intersection statement to compare its generic lengths with the cycle face map; vanishing removes components of excessive codimension. Flat degeneracies use the already owned flat cycle pullback.

The rows from coherent G₀ to the generic cycle groups are surjective, so the generator calculation proves the commutative face squares for the point-supported model. Simplicial identities then come from the original spectra diagram.
For arbitrary morphisms compare both sides on the same good-position refinement; the existing cycle-transfers node supplies the cycle-side independence and composition.
acceptance: All Tor terms have finite length at the relevant generic intersection point, and only finitely many are nonzero because the ambient scheme is regular.
The underlying reduced inverse-image support is insufficient: generic intersection multiplicities must be retained.
Over ℚ, for X=A¹_x and W={s=x²}⊂X×Δ¹_s, restriction to the face s=0 gives 2[0], since ℚ[x]_(x)/(x²) has length two; the other face gives [1]+[−1].

sources.match: Uses derived coherent restriction and Serre intersection multiplicity to prove simplex compatibility, rather than inferring it from the coefficient groups.

nodes.title: The layer is the Eilenberg–MacLane spectrum of the cycle complex
nodes.statement: For every smooth separated finite-type scheme X over a perfect field k and p≥0 there is a natural equivalence of spectra L_K^p(X)≃H(z^p(X,•)), where H sends the homological cycle complex to its Eilenberg–MacLane spectrum and π_m H(C)=H_m(C). Hence π_m L_K^p(X)≅CH^p(X,m)=H^{2p−m}(X,ℤ(p)) for m≥0 and π_m L_K^p(X)=0 for m<0. The equivalence is natural for the functorial tower pullbacks and agrees with open restriction and the supported localisation triangles. It is a layer calculation independent of an exact couple, convergence theorem, Adams operations or rational degeneration.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is a smooth separated scheme of finite type over k; p,n are nonnegative integers.
proofSteps: The pointwise rank maps are equivalences and, by face-rank-compatibility, form a map of simplicial spectra.
Realise that map and use the realisation/Eilenberg–MacLane comparison for a simplicial abelian group. The realised source is the actual adjacent tower cofibre by the point-layer theorem.

Use the imported homotopy-group convention for H and M.4’s definition of the cycle complex. Localisation compatibility follows from restriction on supported coherent classes and M.4’s localisation theorem.
acceptance: For a field F, L_K^0(F)≃Hℤ; π₀ is ℤ and π₁ is zero.
For a field F, π₁L_K^1(F)=CH¹(F,1)≅F×, whereas z¹(F,0)=0. This detects the essential simplex direction.
For X=P¹_k, π₀L_K^1(X)=CH¹(P¹)=ℤ with generator the class of a rational point.

sources.match: Identifies the K-theory coniveau layer with Bloch’s cycle spectrum, including the simplex-compatibility argument.

nodes.title: The global face-exact coherent model
nodes.statement: For Y_n=X×Δ^n and an open V⊂Y_n, let Coh_∂(V) be the full exact subcategory of coherent O_V-modules F for which Tor_i^{O_V}(F,O_{V∩(X×F′)})=0 for every face F′⊂Δ^n and every i>0. Equivalently require Tor-independence for every cosimplicial map into Y_n; codegeneracies are flat. Ordinary restriction to a face is exact on this subcategory and lands in the corresponding face-exact category. Set G_∂^W(Y_n)=hofib(K(Coh_∂(Y_n))→K(Coh_∂(Y_n∖W))) and G_∂^(p)(X,n)=hocolim_{W∈S_X^p(n)}G_∂^W(Y_n). After coherent strictification these form a simplicial spectrum and hence a realised tower. This is Levine’s global coherent homotopy-coniveau model; it is not the naive simplicial object of the unqualified categories Coh_{codim≥p}(X×Δ^n).
hypotheses: X is smooth quasi-projective over the perfect field k for the stated global comparison; p,n≥0.
Exact categories and their K-spectra use the imported essentially-small enhanced models and fixed universes.
proofSteps: Higher Tor vanishing is stable under extensions and kernels of admissible surjections, giving the inherited exact structure. It makes each face pullback exact; composition follows from the derived tensor identities for nested faces.
Use the pseudofunctorial pullback coherences and the requested diagram replacement to form the simplicial exact-category model and its K-spectrum; define supports as actual restriction fibres.

Apply the same admissible support posets and transitions as for the perfect-complex tower. The support formula remains a homotopy fibre, so no unsupported assertion about an exact-category quotient is required.
acceptance: Ordinary pullback is used only on a category where higher Tor vanishes.

sources.locator: §2.2 and Remark 2.3, pp. 8–9; Appendix B.2–B.8, pp. 81–83
sources.match: Defines the face-Tor-independent coherent categories, their simplicial pullbacks, restriction fibres and support families.
Reindexes the global coherent niveau model by codimension.

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.faceExactCoherent_mem

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.faceExactCoherent_pullback

api.name: HomotopyConiveau.faceExactTower

uses.how: Provides the coherent tower to be compared with perfect-complex K.
Resolution compares the restricted coherent categories to ordinary G-theory.
Supplies a global tower model in which boundary and cycle conventions can be checked.

nodes.title: Comparison with Levine’s global tower
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-projective X/k, the derived Cartan maps yield a natural equivalence of towers K^(p)(X)≃G_∂^(p)(X), compatible with support enlargement, the augmentation at p=0, open restriction and layer triangles. In every degree n and for every admissible closed W the map K(Y_n on W)→G_∂^W(Y_n) is an equivalence of spectra. Under this comparison the rank map on layers is the coherent generic-length cycle map. Zariski derived sections give the same tower, rather than merely isomorphic homotopy groups or a matching E₂ page.
hypotheses: k is perfect and X is smooth quasi-projective over k; p,n≥0.
The stronger global coherent comparison for arbitrary regular non-quasi-projective schemes is not asserted by this node.
proofSteps: Quasi-projectivity supplies the resolution property on Y_n and every open complement. Resolve coherent sheaves by finite locally free sheaves, retaining the face-Tor condition on the syzygies. Resolution identifies K(Coh_∂(V)) with the vector-bundle K-spectrum for V=Y_n and V=Y_n∖W.
Use the imported vector-bundle/perfect-complex model comparison. Regularity makes the nonconnective and connective K-spectra agree here; this avoids using only a groupwise Schlichting–TT comparison.

The resolutions and derived restriction commute through the enhanced models. Comparing the restriction fibre squares gives the supported equivalence, then homotopy colimits and realisation give a map of entire towers.
Trace a coherent generic class through the comparison to obtain its length-weighted cycle. Apply the descent theorem to both sides to compare with derived sections.
acceptance: At p=0 the comparison is the regular-scheme Cartan equivalence K(X)≃G(X).
This compares spectra and their tower arrows. Equality of graded groups alone would not meet the target.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.3 and Remark 3.4, p. 13; Appendix B.8–B.9, pp. 83–84
sources.match: The regular K/coherent comparison is termwise and retains supports; the quasi-projective hypothesis here ensures the global resolutions used in that proof.

sources.locator: Proposition A.2 and Remark A.3, p. 81
sources.match: Mayer–Vietoris on a finite-dimensional noetherian space computes derived sections.

nodes.title: Comparison with the Friedlander–Suslin support tower
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-projective X/k, the tower K^(p)(X) is naturally equivalent, with its augmentation and every support-enlargement transition, to the Friedlander–Suslin tower K^{C^p}(Δ^•×X) of (6.0). Here C^p(X,n) is exactly the family of facewise admissible closed supports, and supported K is evaluated on bounded complexes of the big vector bundles of their Appendix C.4–C.5 whose cohomological support lies in an admissible member of that family. This is equivalent to the filtered homotopy colimit over the members. The equivalence also identifies the towers after Zariski derived sections, their stable layer triangles, and the generic-length map to cycles. It compares their global support tower, not an unspecified auxiliary quasi-finite tower.
hypotheses: k is perfect and X is smooth quasi-projective over k; the initially irreducible source convention extends componentwise to smooth X.
Support-family K means complexes supported in some member, equivalently the filtered union over finite admissible support families.
proofSteps: Evaluation of a big vector bundle on X gives an equivalence with ordinary vector bundles; its advantage is that pullback compositions hold strictly. Bounded complexes with quasi-isomorphisms give the imported Waldhausen model of perfect-complex K on these schemes.

The family C^p has the identical facewise codimension condition as S_X^p(n). Finite unions remain admissible. Every bounded complex and every finite diagram in its Waldhausen construction has support in a single admissible finite union. Thus its supported K-spectrum is the filtered homotopy colimit of the single-support K-spectra.

The localisation theorem identifies each single-support model with K(Y_n on W). Its negative groups vanish by the regular-ambient Cartan comparison with connective G(W), so passage from the connective Ω-prespectrum to the nonconnective convention introduces no extra summand.

Make these comparisons on the support diagrams before taking homotopy colimits. They commute with all simplex pullbacks and inclusions C^(p+1)⊂C^p, hence realisation identifies the entire towers. Nisnevich excision gives Zariski descent, so the same maps compare their derived-section presentations.
acceptance: The comparison commutes with K^(p+1)→K^(p) before homotopy groups are taken.
In simplex degree zero it is the imported ordinary codimension-support model; in weight zero it is the regular K-spectrum of X.
The Ω-prespectrum is compared using its entire sequence of deloopings. Its first Waldhausen classifying space is not treated as the underlying spectrum.

sources.match: Defines the support families and the realised support tower independently of the subsequent exact-couple argument.
Gives the big-vector-bundle strict pullback model, supported Waldhausen K and realisation on cosimplicial schemes.

nodes.title: Agreement with the Friedlander–Suslin global cycle layer
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-projective X over a perfect field and p≥0, the layer equivalence identifies L_K^p(X) with RΓ_Zar(X,H C_*z_equi(A^p,0)), where the relative-cycle sheaf z_equi and its Suslin complex are imported from MC.4 and M.5a. Explicitly, use the sheafwise zigzag z^p(−,•)→z^p(−×A^p,•)←C_*z_equi(A^p,0), whose arrows are quasi-isomorphisms. The resulting spectrum is the cycle-layer prespectrum of Friedlander–Suslin’s Proposition 13.10, using all its deloopings. In cohomological notation it is H(RΓ_Zar(X,ℤ(p))[2p]), so π_m=H^{2p−m}(X,ℤ(p)). No extra suspension from their first delooping B is inserted. Together with levine-global-comparison this gives a global supported tower with the same specified cycle layer; it makes no inference of a filtered equivalence from agreement of E₂ pages.
hypotheses: k is perfect, X is smooth quasi-projective over k and p≥0.
The existing MC.4 relative-cycle comparison is an imported target, not a newly planned motivic or relative-cycle theory.
proofSteps: Import the relative-cycle sheaf and its transfers from MC.4; quasi-finite dominant cycles, rather than just finite correspondences, are the required object.

Use MC.4’s Suslin–Friedlander embedding together with homotopy invariance of Bloch’s cycle complex to obtain the displayed sheafwise zigzag. This is precisely the published Friedlander–Suslin Proposition 12.1 comparison.
Apply derived sections and the Eilenberg–MacLane comparison; M.4 descent identifies the Bloch side with global cycles.

Compare the indexing of the entire Ω-prespectrum in Friedlander–Suslin Proposition 13.10, rather than taking its first delooping as the underlying spectrum. This fixes π_m and the cohomological shift.
acceptance: For X=Spec F and p=0 the spectrum is Hℤ, with π₀=ℤ; treating the first B-delooping as the spectrum would wrongly shift this to π₁.
For p=1, n=0, z_equi(A¹,0)(Spec F) is free on closed points of A¹, whereas z¹(F,0)=0. The zigzag is a derived comparison, not a degreewise identification.

requests.need: Extend the sequential-telescope interface to small filtered support posets and simplicial diagrams of ordinary spectra: functorial derived homotopy colimits and realisations, cofinality, π_i of a filtered homotopy colimit, Fubini for bisimplicial realisations, preservation of finite stable fibre/cofibre sequences, and |H A_•|≃H(N A_•) for a simplicial abelian group. Also supply coherent tower/presheaf diagram replacements on a small skeleton of Sm/k, their Nisnevich-local replacements compatible with the S.4 descent interface, finite homotopy-fixed-point averaging after inverting the group order, finite total face-cube fibres, and compatibility of these operations with the imported Ω-prespectrum and Waldhausen presentations of ordinary K-spectra. The existing sequential-homotopy-colimit node alone does not supply these operations. Sources: Levine HCT §§1.6,2.1,4.1,6.3; Levine Moving §§1.3–1.5,7.3.

Construct the algebraic-singular homotopy K-theory KH when needed and supply its closed-cover descent for the normal-crossing boundary D=V(t_0⋯t_n) of the vertex-semilocal simplex R_{n,F}, together with K_i(D)→KH_i(D) for i≤1 (the K₁-regular normal-crossing case used by Levine HCT Theorem 6.4.1, pp. 35–36). In particular identify the multirelative face-cube K₀ group with the ordinary relative KH₀ group and provide exactness K₁(R)→K₁(D)→K₀(R,∂)→K₀(R)→K₀(D). Do not assume ordinary K has closed descent on arbitrary singular unions. The existing S.5 plan explicitly constructs KH only when a consumer needs it; M.6a is such a consumer.

Extend SF.5/tor-intersection beyond its stated algebraically closed base: for a regular ambient scheme essentially smooth over a perfect field, identify proper face intersection cycles with the finite alternating generic Tor-length formula, and supply Serre vanishing for components of excessive codimension. Require compatibility with successive regular simplex-face restrictions and flat degeneracies. This is the cycle-theoretic input to the spectrum rank map, not a construction of Chow theory in M.6a. Source: Levine HCT Theorem 6.4.2, pp. 36–37.

remaining: Discharge the three explicit supplier contracts: general spectrum diagrams/realisation, the normal-crossing KH input for the semilocal criterion, and the general-field Serre–Tor intersection formula. These are requests to the existing owners, not missing M.6a target definitions.

Reconcile the tower, cycle-layer normalisation and global-model comparisons with M.6b’s exact-couple and convergence work at assembly. M.6a establishes no infinite-tower convergence, operations or degeneration.

sourceIssues.printed: In the final rank argument the manuscript identifies the K₀ group of the entire semilocal normal-crossing boundary with a single copy of ℤ. (Paraphrase.)
sourceIssues.correction: Only injectivity of K₀(R)→K₀(R/I) is required. It follows by evaluation at any vertex. For n=1 the boundary ring is F×F, its K₀ is ℤ², and the map is the diagonal ℤ→ℤ². The multirelative K₀ vanishing is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: For R=F[t] semilocalised at t=0,1 and I=(t(1−t)), the two maximal ideals are comaximal; the Chinese remainder theorem gives R/I≅F×F. A vector bundle of rank a restricts with rank a at both vertices.
sourceIssues.known: new: no correction was identified in the versions and searches listed; this does not assert novelty of the observation.
searched: arXiv record and web search for Levine homotopy coniveau tower boundary K₀ correction, 2026-10-19

sourceIssues.printed: After pulling a rank-d normal bundle to its complement of the zero section, the manuscript uses the diagonal nonzero vector to claim a trivialisation of that whole pullback bundle. (Paraphrase.)
sourceIssues.correction: A nonzero vector supplies only a rank-one subbundle. A proof for general theories needs a full frame construction and its descent/independence argument, or an equivalent coordinate-independence proof. This packet uses purity only for explicitly trivialised smooth normal bundles and uses regular-support K-dévis­sage to make the generic rank coefficient independent of the local normal coordinates. It does not import that general canonical-trivialisation step.
sourceIssues.reason: Pullback preserves rank: q*N still has rank d, whereas the claimed trivial line has rank one if d>1. A single vector cannot be a basis of a d-dimensional fibre.
sourceIssues.known: new: no correction was identified in the versions and searches listed; the stated purity conclusion is not declared false.
